figures.Tab12.2: Table 12.2 Properties of some common oxides of nitrogen, Structure column (the table itself is carried as a table block) (PDF page 276). Original figure archived as c11-chem-ch12-fig-tab12-2-oxide-structures (drawn for this lesson after the printed figure; not the textbook's picture). The printed table shows NO as :N≡O: (a triple bond, 10 valence electrons); drawn as N=O with a lone pair and one unpaired electron on N and two lone pairs on O (11 electrons, paramagnetic as the table states) (correct).

findings: The print writes the oxidation-state range as 'I+ to V+' and labels the NO dimer 'Nitrogen dioxide NO, N2O2'; noted.

Table 12.2 prints NO as :N≡O:, which has only 10 valence electrons and contradicts the table's own 'NO is paramagnetic'; the structures figure draws N=O with an unpaired electron on N and the Roman Urdu lesson explains the correction.
